ic_name: IEEE 1149.1 JTAG TAP Controller (TI SSYA002C primer)
test_debug_features: BYPASS — 1-bit short-cut between TDI and TDO; used to shorten the daisy chain when only some devices are being tested.
EXTEST — output BSCs drive board interconnect; input BSCs observe board interconnect; enables open / short / solder-joint / etch testing.
SAMPLE/PRELOAD — snapshot of device I/O pin activity during normal operation (SAMPLE) and pre-load of BSR-drive values before EXTEST (PRELOAD).
INTEST (optional) — in-system functional test of one device's internal logic via BSR-applied stimulus.
IDCODE / USERCODE (optional) — 32-bit device fingerprint readback through the Device Identification register; lets the tester verify device presence + revision + customer-programmed user code.
RUNBIST (optional) — TAP-initiated built-in self-test; result read back via a result register.
CLAMP (optional) — drives outputs from pre-loaded BSR while only the Bypass register is in the shift path; useful when isolating a faulty driver during long bypass-only shifts.
HIGHZ (optional) — places all outputs in high-impedance; helps board-level diagnosis by removing a device's drivers from the bus.
Boundary-Scan Description Language (BSDL) — VHDL-subset description of a device's pin assignments, BSR cell types, and IR opcodes; consumed by test-generation tools.
Hierarchical Scan Description Language (HSDL) — extends BSDL with hierarchical scan-path descriptions for boards-of-boards.
Serial Vector Format (SVF) — vendor-neutral file format for JTAG test vectors; defines a set of TAP-FSM-aware commands (TLR / RTI / SIR / SDR / RUNTEST / PAUSE / ...).
applications_supported_by_jtag_primer: Cluster testing of non-boundary-scan ICs surrounded by boundary-scan devices.
ASIC verification (in-system functional check via INTEST).
Embedded-memory testing (RAM/ROM accessed through the surrounding BS device's BSR).
Backplane multidrop test environment (ring / star configurations).
Embedded applications: device programming + system-level debug + maintenance.
Boundary-scan test flow (automated functional verification + interactive fault isolation).

spec_provided_observability.name: TDO scan output
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Primary observation point; carries the shift output of the selected IR or DR each TCK in ShiftIR/ShiftDR.

spec_provided_observability.name: IR capture pattern (b...b01)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Built-in sanity check: tester loads IDCODE-or-BYPASS, then shifts in CaptureIR pattern, verifies LSBs '01' on TDO to confirm the IR is alive.

spec_provided_observability.name: IDCODE register
spec_provided_observability.purpose: 32-bit device fingerprint readback (when implemented); identifies the device in each slot of the chain.

spec_provided_observability.name: BSR (SAMPLE)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Snapshot of all device boundary pins during normal operation; lets the tester observe in-system pin activity without disturbing the device.

spec_provided_observability.name: BSR (EXTEST input cells)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Observe board-level interconnect: input cells capture the value at the device pin (driven by board / upstream device's EXTEST output).

spec_provided_observability.name: RUNBIST result register
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Reports BIST PASS/FAIL after the BIST completes in RunTestIdle (when RUNBIST is supported).

spec_provided_controllability: BSR (EXTEST output cells) drives each output pin from a tester-shifted value — direct control of every output without using functional inputs.
BSR (INTEST input cells) drives the device's internal logic with tester-shifted stimulus — slow ATE-style functional test.
HIGHZ removes the device's drivers from board buses for fault isolation.
CLAMP holds the output pins at the pre-loaded BSR values during long bypass-only shifts.
fault_models_detected_by_jtag: Short to ground / short to VDD.
Missing component (drives default to pull-up/pull-down → detected by EXTEST).
Wrong orientation (BSR pin mapping mismatches at IDCODE-compare time).
notes: IEEE 1149.1 fundamentally splits test architecture into mandatory (BYPASS + EXTEST + SAMPLE/PRELOAD + the 16-state TAP + Bypass + BSR) and optional (INTEST / RUNBIST / CLAMP / HIGHZ / IDCODE / USERCODE + Device Identification register + user-defined data registers). The mandatory set alone is enough for interconnect-test and board-level fault isolation; the optional set adds in-system functional test, BIST automation, device identification, and bus isolation.
